title: ci-ok waits for every job and fails when one didn't do what was expected
assertion: In every `.github/workflows/swerepo-ci.yml` that `swerepo init` writes (with ruff, kept linters, a gradual move to ruff, the governance job, per-project jobs, and jobs asked for on a later run), `ci-ok` runs `if: always()` and its `needs:` names every other job. Run with GitHub's results for those jobs, its step passes only when every job succeeded or was skipped by design (test-macos off pushes, governance off pull requests, dependency-review off pull requests to public repositories), and exits non-zero when any job failed, was cancelled, was skipped unexpectedly, or ran when it should have been skipped.

origin.text: ADR-20261122-4a06 (Phase 4): the ruleset requires only ci-ok, so a job ci-ok doesn't wait for, or a failure it lets through, wouldn't block a merge. Strengthened after SeamSpec's reviewer: the test runs ci-ok's own step on sample results; the Python-versions promise moved to its own rule.
